# LoCoMo: very long-term conversational memory (Maharana et al., ACL 2024)
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17753 (HTML read; Sec 3 generation pipeline, Sec 4 benchmark, intro findings).

**Problem.** Evaluate dialogue models on conversations 9x longer than MSC.

**Data model.** 10 long conversations (up to 35 sessions, ~9K tokens per the A-Mem description; ~300 turns), generated by two LLM agents with personas and a **temporal event graph** per agent, then human-edited (about 15% of turns changed) (Sec 3.1-3.4). Multimodal (image sharing).

**Tasks.** QA with five categories (single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain/commonsense, adversarial), event-graph summarisation (FactScore), multimodal dialogue generation (Sec 4).

**Findings.** RAG/long-context improve QA by 22-66% but lag humans by 56% overall and **73% on temporal reasoning**; long-context models are 83% worse on adversarial questions (misassign events to speakers); RAG does best when dialogue is converted to a database of assertions ("observations") per speaker (intro finding 3).

**Critique from later work.** Memora (2604.20006 Intro): 94% of LoCoMo questions need evidence from at most two earlier sessions, so it measures shallow retrieval; the Zep authors and Mem0 authors dispute each other's LoCoMo numbers (Mem0 2504.19413 Table 1 vs a Zep blog reported by search, unverified). Because scores come from different judges and category definitions, cross-paper LoCoMo numbers (A-Mem F1, Mem0 J, RippleMem J 87.14, REALM 75.97, Agent Zero 93.6) are not comparable.

**What neocortex could steal.** Use LoCoMo's per-speaker "observation" idea: for each conversation turn, retrieval over agent-supplied assertions beats raw turns for single-hop/temporal. neocortex already stores assertions when `remember` receives entities/relations; for text-only memories the rules tier could emit speaker-attributed observations (`extract_model.rs`). Treat the event graph as a *gold* for a temporal-ordering eval (the benchmark ships events with dates): it directly tests TM-12 (ordering/duration). Do not tune on category F1 numbers.

**Weak / wrong.** LLM-generated, shallow evidence depth, label noise in categories, short for "months". Adversarial category counts abstention.
